title: Standardize traffic synthesis and sunset legacy adapters
creator: Samira Patel
description: Background: Over the last 18 months the perf and load harness has accreted multiple traffic synthesizers and adapter shims (node-runner v1, java-proxy shim, legacy benchlib) which produce slightly different distributions of sequence length, client-side pacing, and inferred user tokenization. This has made perf regressions noisy and increased CI flakiness. Goal: replace the heterogeneous synthesizers with a single, configurable traffic-synthesis library that emits deterministic, statistically-parameterized workloads, and deprecate/sunset legacy adapters while preserving historical regression comparators.
acceptance_criteria: A single traffic-synthesis library (bench-synth v2) is available as a test dependency and used by all perf/regression scenarios
Legacy adapter shims (node-runner v1, java-proxy shim, benchlib-legacy) are disabled behind feature flags and a migration guide exists
Regression CI jobs show reduced 95th-percentile variance by at least 30% on the canonical kernel/sequence-length matrix
Deterministic seeding and reproducible corpora are stored as artifacts for every regression run
Migration runbook and compatibility tests for Dedicated and Private customers are published and reviewed by Platform and Console teams
plan: Prototype bench-synth v2 that supports: poisson and bursty arrival patterns, token-length distributions, client-side pacing jitter model, and deterministic seed control
Add a lightweight compatibility layer that maps legacy adapter configs to the new canonical workload spec
Introduce feature flags to gate legacy adapters and run a 2-week shadow period comparing outputs
Update CI pipeline steps: replace legacy runners with bench-synth invocations, persist seed+corpora artifacts, and add variance monitoring dashboards
Coordinate with infra to upgrade bench-runner image to include the new library and runtime dependencies
Prepare migration guide and schedule opportunistic sunset of legacy adapters after the shadow period and sign-off
updates: 2026-02-25: Spike complete — bench-synth prototype emits configurable token-length histograms and supports deterministic seeds (Samira)
2026-03-02: Compatibility layer draft pushed in https://github.com/redwood-inference/bench-synth/pull/13; initial smoke tests against ENG-32145 scenarios (Marco)
2026-03-05: Observed reduced variance in short-sequence matrix but increased tail for bursty traffic; identified pacing jitter model mismatch (Investigation by Marco and Linnea)
2026-03-09: Implemented pacing jitter correction and added a back-pressure knob to match legacy runner burst behavior; re-ran regression and saw 32% reduction in 95p variance for canonical matrix
2026-03-12: Opened CI migration PRs to swap runner image and upload seeds/artifacts to GCS. Begin 2-week shadow run on nightly jobs (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ci/pull/488)
comments: Samira Patel (2026-02-26): Spike results look promising. Next up: add config to express 'burstiness' vs Poisson and a seed export format that can be checked into artifacts.
Marco Silva (2026-03-03): Compatibility layer maps 90% of legacy configs; remaining differences due to tokenization edge cases — need a tokenizer-normalization step.
Linnea Berg (2026-03-06): Noted increased tail under heavy bursts — will prototype pacing jitter fix and add an exponential backoff option to the client-side model.
Aisha Kumar (QA) (2026-03-10): Please add an acceptance test that compares token-level generation timings across legacy and new runners to avoid semantic regressions.
Marco Silva (2026-03-12): Shadow run started. We'll collect two weeks of nightly runs and then propose sunset for legacy adapters on 2026-04-05 if no regressions are detected.
notes: Trade-off: Keeping a compatibility layer increases maintenance but drastically reduces migration friction for downstream scenarios; we favor this to avoid one-off rewrites.
Decision: Deterministic seeds will be 128-bit hex strings and exported as artifacts attached to CI runs to enable exact reruns for debugging.
Risk: Dedicated/private customers with custom on-prem adapters may require a longer deprecation window — coordinate with Customer Success for bespoke plans.
Follow-ups: Add a lightweight statistical monitor that alerts when regression job variance increases beyond historical baselines (ENG-? new ticket).
